description: We are planning to design a 2d space mission simulator using the data provided by NASA.
summary:
Fifteen Days on Mars is ,very much self explanatory, a Mars simulation themed strategy video game. You as an astronaut have to manage the mission with limited resources, using real planetary data provided by NASA. Across 15 Martian days, player have to complete the daily tasks assigned by an alien friend, using specialized tools to navigate terrain, manage vital resources, and survive Mars's harsh environment. It requires real problem solving skills and the responsibility it takes to manage the mission.
  
When it comes to the importance; NASA collects a large amounts of public data, yet a hard on terms, too scientific research papers often feel intimidating or for general public. We believe by transforming the data set into a Mars space mission game will bridge the gaps between scientific and complex space science and everyday entertainment. Designed for younger learners, space enthusiasts, and casual gamers alike; with this simulation it's possible to spark curiosity in younger generations and empower regular people to intuitively understand the real challenges of a human driven space mission.
details:
We made ''Fifteen Days on Mars'' to be a survival strategy game where the player will try to live on Mars and make it back home. The game starts with an animation of a spaceship flight to Mars, followed by a setup phase where you have a limited budget to pick your spaceship and buy helpful buffs. Once the astronaut land, an alien named Zip will give you a quick rundown of information and set of daily tasks you will need to complete.

You, the player, will have to manage habitat which is basically a space base and keep your resources from running out. If you fail, you lose and you will have to start all over again. You work with a habitat, a greenhouse, a water tank, an ice breaker, rock-analyzing tools, and other gear to stay alive. At the end of each day, a set of science questions will be given and you have to answer them before moving on. You have to survive 15 full days like this before you can launch back to Earth.

NASA has a large amount of database about Mars, but looking at those raw numbers and way too scientific reports may get boring for a regular person. Our game takes that real information and turns it into an actual strategy game you can play. We especially target the younger generations and space enthusiasts, and our main goal is to strike while the iron is hot: using popular gaming culture to get kids and teens excited about space exploration when young. Whether you are a student, a space fan, or just someone looking for a fun challenge, this game shows what a space mission takes while making NASA's public data easy for anyone to understand.

For the codes we used, we started to practise on Unity (C#) but found javascript more suiting for our game logic. So during the hackathon we used the knowledge gained from our practises and and merged it into Visual Studio. During the process we did not use any files,a ssets or sounds made outside the hackathon; but to improve efficency we got help from Claude Code. For musics and assets we used BandLab and IbisPaint. After the data anlysis to organise our notes we also used Claude.

Instead of making a plain chart or a boring quiz app; we mixed resource management, budget planning, and engagingly fun guiding with real NASA science. We also made sure of anyone could easily play our game since accessibility is a must for our target audience. That is why we built versions for both desktop computers and web browsers, so people can play right away without needing an expensive PC.
